ca_1_prowler_area.blurb: Prowler Area is a small group of boulders on the hillside of Conejo Mountain in Newbury Park, part of the wider Conejo Boulders. It has nine problems between V0 and V3, with most of them at the easier end. The stones are spread along a ravine and a short climber's trail, and a few lines sit on a boulder in the creek bed on the way up. Holds can be sharp in places and crumbly in others, so test flakes before pulling hard. It works well for a short session rather than a full day, and it can be strung together with the neighboring Lost Gully for a longer circuit.

ca_alien_wall.blurb: Alien Wall is a sport wall in the Central Gorge section of the Owens River Gorge, near Bishop, standing next to the power plant. The face is made up of several pink slabs, and two large boulders on the scree slope below carry a few more lines. There are nine routes: eight sport and one trad, spanning 5.9 to 5.12. Most fall at 5.9 and 5.10, with two at 5.12, so it suits climbers working through the middle grades. The Central Gorge around it is the busiest part of the gorge.

ca_traverse_wall_backside_southwest_face.blurb: This stretch of Indian Rock Park in Berkeley sits to the right of the pit by the park entrance, beginning where the pegboard wall ends. It has nine lines: eight boulder problems and one top-rope climb. Most of the problems run from V0 to V2, with two at V5, including the Indian Rock Traverse. The left-hand problems are short, while the ones further right grow tall enough that a rope may be wanted. Parts of the rock are overgrown, and it sees fewer climbers than the main bouldering area down the stairs.

ca_comic_strip_sw_face_the.blurb: The Comic Strip is a large formation in the Comic Book Area of Central Joshua Tree, visible from Hidden Valley Campground. Its tall main face reaches about 250 feet and holds several multi-pitch routes. There are nine climbs: eight trad and one sport. Grades cluster around 5.10, with one climb near 5.8, one at 5.9 and one at 5.11. Most trad lines are two pitches of cracks and face climbing, so bring a standard rack and a partner comfortable on 5.10 leads.
ca_comic_strip_sw_face_the.parking_note: Several turnouts line the Bighorn Pass Road roughly half a mile beyond Echo Tee; leave the car in any of them.
ca_comic_strip_sw_face_the.approach: A marked trail heads along the hillside from the roadside turnouts to the formation. Allow roughly 15 to 20 minutes.

ca_thin_wall_east_face_right.blurb: This is the right-hand section of the Thin Wall in Real Hidden Valley, Joshua Tree National Park. It has nine trad climbs, mostly moderate cracks. Grades run from 5.6 to 5.9, with four at 5.8 and one climb on easier ground, so it suits climbers building up their crack skills and placing gear on friendly terrain. The Thin Wall as a whole draws beginners in numbers, so arriving early or late helps avoid a wait at the popular cracks.
ca_thin_wall_east_face_right.approach: Follow the nature trail from the Real Hidden Valley parking lot to the wall, about 10 to 15 minutes.

ca_dos_equis_wall.blurb: Dos Equis Wall is a sheer, dark face in Indian Cove, in Joshua Tree National Park. It has nine trad routes, and most are on the longer side with real exposure. Grades lean toward 5.10: five routes sit there, with one each around 5.7, 5.8, 5.11 and 5.12. That makes it a fit for climbers who already lead 5.10 cracks and faces with confidence. A single-rope rappel from bolts atop one of the harder lines gets you back to the base.
ca_dos_equis_wall.approach: Hike and scramble up the rocky gully beside the formation to reach the foot of the wall.
